title: AS2: string \xNN and \uXXXX escape sequences produce wrong output
description: The tokenizer (packages/core/src/as2/tokenizer.ts:91) copies the raw char-after-backslash without decoding hex escapes. The parser string literal handler (parser.ts:1032) replaces \n, \t, \r, \', \", \\ but NOT \xNN hex escapes or \uXXXX unicode escapes. So var s = '\x41' produces the 4-char literal '\x41' instead of 'A', and '\u0041' produces a 6-char literal instead of 'A'. Fix: in the string literal parser, add cases for \x (read 2 hex digits, decode to char) and \u (read 4 hex digits, decode to UTF-16 char). String.fromCharCode(parseInt('41', 16)) pattern. Also add an \0 (null char) case. The test at stringliterals.test.ts:63 only calls compilesOk — add assertions checking the decoded byte value.
